blocks.path: Blepharitis
s: Blepharitis causes swollen, itchy eyelids.
It's not usually serious and can often be treated by washing your eyelids every day.

blocks.path: Blepharitis > Symptoms of blepharitis
s: Blepharitis symptoms often come and go.

blocks.path: Blepharitis > Symptoms of blepharitis
s: Symptoms of blepharitis include:

blocks.path: Blepharitis > Symptoms of blepharitis
s: sore eyelids

blocks.path: Blepharitis > Symptoms of blepharitis
s: itchy eyes

blocks.path: Blepharitis > Symptoms of blepharitis
s: a gritty feeling in the eyes

blocks.path: Blepharitis > Symptoms of blepharitis
s: flakes or crusts around the roots of the eyelashes

blocks.path: Blepharitis > Symptoms of blepharitis
s: eyelids sticking together in the morning when you wake up

blocks.path: Blepharitis > Symptoms of blepharitis > If you're not sure it's blepharitis
s: Find out more about eyelid problems

blocks.path: Blepharitis > Things you can do to treat and prevent blepharitis > Do clean your eyelids twice a day continue to clean your eyes, even if your symptoms clear up Don’t
s: do not wear contact lenses while you have symptoms

blocks.path: Blepharitis > Things you can do to treat and prevent blepharitis > Do clean your eyelids twice a day continue to clean your eyes, even if your symptoms clear up Don’t
s: do not use eye makeup, especially eyeliner and mascara, while you have symptoms

blocks.path: Blepharitis > Things you can do to treat and prevent blepharitis > How to clean your eyes
s: Soak a clean flannel or cotton wool in warm water and place it on your closed eyelid for 5 to 10 minutes.

blocks.path: Blepharitis > Things you can do to treat and prevent blepharitis > How to clean your eyes
s: Gently massage your eyelids for around 30 seconds.

blocks.path: Blepharitis > Things you can do to treat and prevent blepharitis > How to clean your eyes
s: Clean your eyelids using cotton wool or a cotton bud.
It might help to use a small amount of baby shampoo in water.
Gently wipe along the edge of your eyelids to remove any flakes or crusts.

blocks.path: Blepharitis > Things you can do to treat and prevent blepharitis > A pharmacist can help with blepharitis
s: A pharmacist might be able to suggest things to help keep your eyelids clean, including:

blocks.path: Blepharitis > Things you can do to treat and prevent blepharitis > A pharmacist can help with blepharitis
s: eye pads and wipes

blocks.path: Blepharitis > Things you can do to treat and prevent blepharitis > A pharmacist can help with blepharitis
s: eyedrops

blocks.path: Blepharitis > Non-urgent advice: See a GP if:
s: blepharitis symptoms do not improve, or get worse

blocks.path: Blepharitis > Treatment for blepharitis from a GP
s: A GP might suggest using an antibiotic cream or ointment that you rub on your eyelid if your blepharitis does not clear up after cleaning your eyelids regularly.

blocks.path: Blepharitis > Treatment for blepharitis from a GP
s: If blepharitis has caused other problems, such as a lump of fluid under the skin (cyst), antibiotic eyedrops or tablets may be recommended.

blocks.path: Blepharitis > Treatment for blepharitis from a GP
s: If your blepharitis is severe, or if you also have other eye symptoms, the GP may refer you to an eye specialist (ophthalmologist).

blocks.path: Blepharitis > Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent GP appointment or get help from NHS 111 if you have:
s: pain in your eyes

blocks.path: Blepharitis > Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent GP appointment or get help from NHS 111 if you have:
s: changes to your vision, such as vision loss or blurred vision

blocks.path: Blepharitis > Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent GP appointment or get help from NHS 111 if you have:
s: very red eyes

blocks.path: Blepharitis > Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent GP appointment or get help from NHS 111 if you have:
s: These can be signs of a more serious eye problem.

blocks.path: Blepharitis > Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent GP appointment or get help from NHS 111 if you have:
s: You can call 111 or get help from 111 online.

blocks.path: Blepharitis > Causes of blepharitis
s: Blepharitis can be caused by:

blocks.path: Blepharitis > Causes of blepharitis
s: a type of bacteria that lives on the skin

blocks.path: Blepharitis > Causes of blepharitis
s: a skin condition, such as seborrhoeic dermatitis

blocks.path: Blepharitis > Causes of blepharitis
s: the glands inside the eyelids not producing enough oil

blocks.path: Blepharitis > Causes of blepharitis
s: Blepharitis cannot be spread to other people.
